claim: Sonic hedgehog (Shh) expression in the limb bud organizing centre called the zone of polarizing activity is regulated by the ZRS enhancer.
source: Sonic hedgehog (Shh) expression in the limb bud organizing centre called the zone of polarizing activity is regulated by the ZRS enhancer.
evidence: This is a foundational statement supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling in the distal limb primes the ZRS at early embryonic stages maintaining a poised, but inactive state broadly across the distal limb mesenchyme.
source: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling in the distal limb primes the ZRS at early embryonic stages maintaining a poised, but inactive state broadly across the distal limb mesenchyme.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including ChIP experiments and limb culture assays.

claim: The E26 transformation-specific transcription factor, ETV4, which is induced by FGF signalling and acts as a repressor of ZRS activity, interacts with the histone deacetylase HDAC2.
source: The E26 transformation-specific transcription factor, ETV4, which is induced by FGF signalling and acts as a repressor of ZRS activity, interacts with the histone deacetylase HDAC2 and ensures that the poised ZRS remains transcriptionally inactive.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments and ChIP data showing ETV4-HDAC2 interaction.

claim: GABPα, an activator of the ZRS, recruits p300, which is associated with histone acetylation (H3K27ac) indicative of an active enhancer.
source: Conversely, GABPα, an activator of the ZRS, recruits p300, which is associated with histone acetylation (H3K27ac) indicative of an active enhancer.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data and co-immunoprecipitation experiments showing GABPα-p300 interaction.

claim: A highly conserved ~780 bp enhancer called the ZRS controls the spatiotemporal expression of the Shh gene in the ZPA of both the fore and hind limbs.
source: A highly conserved ~780 bp enhancer called the ZRS controls the spatiotemporal expression of the Shh gene in the ZPA of both the fore and hind limbs (Lettice et al., 2002; 2003; Sagai et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The ZRS lies in an intron of the ubiquitously expressed Lmbr1 gene at a distance of 1 Mb from the Shh gene in human.
source: The ZRS lies in an intron of the ubiquitously expressed Lmbr1 gene at a distance of 1 Mb from the Shh gene in human.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genomic location of the ZRS.

claim: Well over 20 different point mutations occurring in the ZRS are associated with the misregulation of Shh and consequently, to limb skeletal defects.
source: Well over 20 different point mutations occurring in the ZRS are associated with the misregulation of Shh and consequently, to limb skeletal defects. These include preaxial polydactyly type 2 (PPD2), triphalangeal thumb polysyndactyly, syndactyly type IV, and Werner's mesomelic syndrome, collectively referred to as ZRS-associated syndromes (Lettice et al., 2003, Lettice et al., 2008; Farooq et al., 2010; Furniss et al., 2008; Gurnett et al., 2007; Semerci et al., 2009; Wieczorek et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies documenting these mutations.

claim: H3K4me1 is a predictive chromatin signature for both poised and active enhancers in the human genome.
source: H3K4me1 is a predictive chromatin signature for both poised and active enhancers in the human genome (Heintzman et al., 2007), but in association with H3K27ac, these mark active regulatory elements (Rada-Iglesias et al., 2012; Cotney et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on histone modifications.

claim: H3K4me1 in association with H3K27ac marks active regulatory elements.
source: H3K4me1 is a predictive chromatin signature for both poised and active enhancers in the human genome (Heintzman et al., 2007), but in association with H3K27ac, these mark active regulatory elements (Rada-Iglesias et al., 2012; Cotney et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on histone modifications.

claim: H3K4me1 was enriched at the ZRS in the distal region of the dissected E11.5 limb buds, which was appreciably lower in the proximal region of the limb buds.
source: We found specific enrichment of H3K4me1 at the ZRS in the distal region of the dissected E11.5 limb buds, which was appreciably lower in the proximal region of the limb buds.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Even though Shh was not expressed in the anterior region of the limb bud, the H3K4me1 mark was enriched in both dissected halves suggesting that the ZRS was poised across the distal compartment of the limb.
source: Even though Shh was not expressed in the anterior region of the limb bud, the H3K4me1 mark was enriched in both dissected halves suggesting that the ZRS was poised across the distal compartment of the limb.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data from anterior and posterior limb dissections shown in Figure 1B.

claim: H3K27ac was differentially enriched in the distal mesenchyme which was greater in the posterior portion of the limb bud.
source: H3K27ac, in contrast, was differentially enriched in the distal mesenchyme which was greater in the posterior portion of the limb bud.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The ZRS encompasses two distinct regulatory activities; one residing in the 5' half driving spatiotemporal expression and one residing in the 3' half mediating long-range activation of the Shh gene.
source: The ZRS encompasses two distinct regulatory activities; one residing in the 5' half driving spatiotemporal expression and one residing in the 3' half mediating long-range activation of the Shh gene (Lettice et al., 2014) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: PCR primers complementary to the 5' spatiotemporal half of the ZRS showed an increase in H3 acetylation compared to the 3' long-range end.
source: Analysis of each half of the enhancer after ChIP identified differential acetylation of H3 across the ZRS. PCR primers complementary to the 5' spatiotemporal half (5'ST primers) of the ZRS showed an increase in H3 acetylation compared to the 3' long-range (3'LR primers) end.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: H3K27ac was associated with the 5' end of the ZRS and was enriched in the distal region of the limb bud.
source: H3K27ac was associated with the 5' end of the ZRS and was enriched in the distal region of the limb bud.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: H3K27ac was associated with the distal, posterior quadrant of the limb bud consistent with the presence of the ZPA where the Shh gene is transcriptionally active.
source: H3K27ac was, therefore, associated with the distal, posterior quadrant of the limb bud consistent with the presence of the ZPA where the Shh gene is transcriptionally active (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data and the known location of the ZPA.

claim: The pattern of the H3K4me1 covered the extent of the ZRS.
source: The pattern of the H3K4me1 covered the extent of the ZRS; whereas, the pattern of H3K27ac, as predicted by the PCR primers, was not centred over the ZRS but was skewed toward the 5' side.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The pattern of H3K27ac was not centred over the ZRS but was skewed toward the 5' side.
source: The pattern of the H3K4me1 covered the extent of the ZRS; whereas, the pattern of H3K27ac, as predicted by the PCR primers, was not centred over the ZRS but was skewed toward the 5' side.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The ZRS exists in differential chromatin states in the limb depending on position and gene activity.
source: Thus, the ZRS exists in differential chromatin states in the limb depending on position and gene activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential patterns of H3K4me1 and H3K27ac observed in different regions of the limb.

claim: RNA-seq analysis of the 14Fp cell line shows that many of the key genes found in the posterior limb bud are expressed with a notable exception being Shh.
source: RNA-seq analysis of the 14Fp cell line (cells derived from the distal/posterior part of the limb at E 11.5) shows that many of the key genes found in the posterior limb bud are expressed with a notable exception being Shh (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: H3K4me1 marked the full extent of the ZRS in the 14Fp cell line.
source: We performed ChIP-on-chip using antibodies against H3K4me1 and H3K27ac which revealed that, H3K4me1 marked the full extent of the ZRS in the cell line; whereas, H3K27ac was not enriched, demonstrating that the ZRS resides in a poised state reflecting the origin of the cell line from the distal mesenchyme of the limb bud (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: H3K27ac was not enriched at the ZRS in the 14Fp cell line, demonstrating that the ZRS resides in a poised state reflecting the origin of the cell line from the distal mesenchyme of the limb bud.
source: We performed ChIP-on-chip using antibodies against H3K4me1 and H3K27ac which revealed that, H3K4me1 marked the full extent of the ZRS in the cell line; whereas, H3K27ac was not enriched, demonstrating that the ZRS resides in a poised state reflecting the origin of the cell line from the distal mesenchyme of the limb bud (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data shown in Figure 2A and inference about the poised state.

claim: The drug trichostatin A (TSA), a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, stimulated Shh expression in the 14Fp cell line.
source: Our attempts with known Shh activators confirmed these observations (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A); however, the drug trichostatin A (TSA), a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, stimulated expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Shh expression was detectable within 6 hr of TSA treatment reaching a maximum at ~24 hr.
source: Shh expression was detectable within 6 hr of treatment (Figure 2B) reaching a maximum at ~24 hr.
evidence: This is supported by time course qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: H3K27ac enrichment was observed over both the ZRS and the Shh promoter at 16 hr of TSA treatment, reaching a maximum at 24 hr.
source: To further investigate Shh activation in the cell line, we carried out a TSA time course to assay H3K27ac enrichment at the ZRS. H3K27ac enrichment was observed over both the ZRS and the Shh promoter at 16 hr of treatment, reaching a maximum at 24 hr (Figure 2C), accordingly, with the Shh expression time course (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR time course data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The correlation between Shh induction of expression and recruitment of H3K27ac suggests that the ZRS is involved in the activation of the transcriptional process.
source: In the cell lines, the correlation between Shh induction of expression and recruitment of H3K27ac suggests that the ZRS is involved in the activation of the transcriptional process.
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal correlation between H3K27ac enrichment and Shh expression.

claim: H3K27ac was more highly associated with the region involved in the spatiotemporal activity of the ZRS.
source: In addition H3K27ac was more highly associated with the region involved in the spatiotemporal activity of the ZRS (as shown using the 5'ST primers).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data using different primer sets shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In the E14 and MD cell lines, the histone mark, H3K4me1, was not enriched over the ZRS, and TSA treatment did not lead to Shh induction after 24 hr of treatment.
source: In both cell lines, the histone mark, H3K4me1, was not enriched over the ZRS, and TSA treatment did not lead to Shh induction after 24 hr of treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B–C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B–C.

claim: Extragenic transcription sites correlate with active regulatory elements and in accord are occupied by RNA Pol II.
source: Extragenic transcription sites correlate with active regulatory elements and in accord are occupied by RNA Pol II (De Santa et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the untreated 14Fp cell line, even though the enhancer is in a poised state, Pol II was not appreciably enriched at the Shh promoter nor at the ZRS.
source: In the untreated 14Fp cell line, even though the enhancer is in a poised state, Pol II was not appreciably enriched at the Shh promoter nor at the ZRS (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data for Pol II shown in Figure 2D.

claim: After activation with TSA, Pol II was detected at both the ZRS and the Shh promoter.
source: After activation with TSA, Pol II was detected at both sites confirming the association of Pol II recruitment to the enhancer and the promoter, further suggesting that TSA mediated Shh activation in 14Fp involves the ZRS.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data for Pol II shown in Figure 2D.

claim: 4C-seq analysis in the 14Fp cell line showed marked and highly signiﬁcant ZRS–Shh interactions in the TSA treated cells.
source: 4C-seq analysis in the 14Fp cell line (Figure 3A) showed marked and highly signiﬁcant ZRS–Shh interactions in the TSA treated cells.
evidence: This is supported by 4C-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The fragment containing the promoter site of Shh co-localizes with the ZRS and was detected at 18 and at 24 hr after TSA treatment.
source: The fragment containing the promoter site of Shh co-localizes with the ZRS and was detected at 18 and at 24 hr after TSA treatment (TSA minus: q < 1.5×10−5; TSA18hr: q-value <5×10−10; TSA+24hr: q < 7.8×10−35); whereas, signiﬁcant contact in the fragment containing the promoter was undetectable in the untreated cells.
evidence: This is supported by 4C-seq data shown in Figure 3A with statistical significance values.

claim: In TSA treated cells reorganization in chromatin structure occurs due to activation of the ZRS increasing interactions with the promoter.
source: Shh/ZRS proximity in the nucleus occurs regardless of whether the gene or enhancer is active (Williamson et al., 2016); however, in TSA treated cells reorganization in chromatin structure occurs due to activation of the ZRS increasing interactions with the promoter.
evidence: This is inferred from the 4C-seq data showing increased interactions upon TSA treatment.

claim: Fgf10 expression in the distal limb bud mesenchyme is important for both limb bud outgrowth and induction of FGF signalling from the AER.
source: At an early stage of limb development, Fgf10 expression in the distal limb bud mesenchyme is important for both limb bud outgrowth and induction of FGF signalling from the AER (Ohuchi et al., 1997) which, in turn, maintains the cells of the progress zone.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: FGFs function to maintain Shh expression in the ZPA.
source: Subsequently, the FGFs function to maintain Shh expression in the ZPA (Laufer et al., 1994; Niswander et al., 1994; Crossley et al., 1996; Vogel et al., 1996; Ohuchi et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The 14Fp cell line pre-treated with nintedanib (NIN), a potent broad spectrum inhibitor of FGFR1/2/3, VEGFR1/2/3, and PDGFRα/β, showed a significant reduction in Shh after TSA treatment.
source: Firstly, the 14Fp cell line pre-treated with nintedanib (NIN), a potent broad spectrum inhibitor of FGFR1/2/3, VEGFR1/2/3, and PDGFRα/β (Hilberg et al., 2008), showed a significant reduction in Shh after TSA treatment (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: An increase in AER-FGF levels leads to gradual repression of Grem1 in the distal mesenchyme as part of an inhibitory feedback loop.
source: Previous studies show that an increase in AER-FGF levels leads to gradual repression of Grem1 in the distal mesenchyme as part of an inhibitory feedback loop (Fgf/Grem1 loop) (Verheyden and Sun, 2008) and promotes expression of Etv4 (Mao et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Increased levels of Grem1 were observed after 4 hr of NIN and BGJ incubations while Etv4 levels were reduced.
source: Increased levels of Grem1 were observed after 4 hr of NIN and BGJ incubations while Etv4 levels were reduced.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The FGF8/10 treatment was sufficient to restore the original levels of both Grem1 and Etv4.
source: The FGF8/10 treatment was sufficient to restore the original levels of both Grem1 and Etv4.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The H3K4me1 enrichment over the ZRS was dramatically reduced after inhibition of FGF activity and TSA treatment did not rescue the presence of this histone modification.
source: The H3K4me1 enrichment over the ZRS was dramatically reduced after inhibition of FGF activity and TSA treatment did not rescue the presence of this histone modification; whereas, Rbm33 intron 1 was not significantly affected.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Distal tips of E11.5 limb buds exposed to NIN for 4 hr lost ZRS enrichment of H3K4me1.
source: In agreement with the cell line results, the distal tips lost ZRS enrichment of H3K4me1 and higher levels of Grem1 expression were observed (Figure 4F–G).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data from limb explants shown in Figure 4G.

claim: When proximal dissections of E11.5 limb bud are exposed to a combination of FGF8 and FGF10 the ZRS displays the poised state showing enrichment of H3K4me1.
source: On the other hand, when proximal dissections of E11.5 limb bud, where the enhancer is in an inactive state, are exposed to a combination of FGF8 and FGF10 the ZRS displays the poised state (Figure 4H, Figure 4—figure supplement 1F) showing enrichment of H3K4me1.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data from limb explants shown in Figure 4H.

claim: FGF signalling has a key role in priming and maintaining the ZRS as a poised enhancer in the distal mesenchyme of the limb bud.
source: These data suggest that FGF signalling has a key role in priming and maintaining the ZRS as a poised enhancer in the distal mesenchyme of the limb bud, delineating the boundaries where Shh can be potentially expressed.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing FGF inhibition reduces H3K4me1 and FGF treatment induces H3K4me1.

claim: GABPα interacts with the ZRS in the limb bud and activates Shh expression.
source: One of these, GABPα, interacts with the ZRS in the limb bud and activates Shh expression.
evidence: This is supported by previous work cited and data in this manuscript.

claim: GABPα recruits the co-activator histone acetyltransferase (HAT) CBP/p300.
source: In addition others have demonstrated (Kang et al., 2008) that GABPα recruits the co-activator histone acetyltransferase (HAT) CBP/p300.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: ChIP-on-chip analysis on untreated 14Fp cells for both GABPα and p300 showed an overlapping peak of enrichment for both factors, suggesting a co-occupancy over the ZRS.
source: ChIP-on-chip analysis on untreated cells for both GABPα and p300 showed an overlapping peak of enrichment for both factors, suggesting a co-occupancy over the ZRS.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of endogenous p300 co-precipitates the flag-GABPα indicating an association between these two factors.
source: Immunoprecipitation of endogenous p300 co-precipitates the flag-GABPα indicating an association between these two factors (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Gabpα siRNA knockdown revealed decreased Shh expression after TSA treatment.
source: Gabpα small interfering RNA (siRNA) knockdown (Figure 5C) revealed decreased Shh expression after TSA treatment (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by siRNA knockdown and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: Overexpression of Gabpα using a doxycycline inducible vector leads to activation of Shh.
source: Conversely, overexpression of Gabpα using a doxycycline inducible vector leads to activation of Shh (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by overexpression and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: ChIP analysis for H3K27ac in cells overexpressing GABPα showed an appreciable enrichment over the ZRS.
source: In addition, ChIP analysis for H3K27ac in cells overexpressing GABPα showed an appreciable enrichment over the ZRS; whereas, the transcription factor ETV4, a repressor (see below) which restricts expression outside the ZPA, is displaced from the ZRS (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: In cells overexpressing GABPα, the transcription factor ETV4 is displaced from the ZRS.
source: In addition, ChIP analysis for H3K27ac in cells overexpressing GABPα showed an appreciable enrichment over the ZRS; whereas, the transcription factor ETV4, a repressor (see below) which restricts expression outside the ZPA, is displaced from the ZRS (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Enrichment of GABPα and p300 over the ZRS is observed in cells overexpressing GABPα.
source: Under these conditions, enrichment of GABPα and p300 over the ZRS is also observed (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: GABPα regulates Shh expression by modulating the acetylation status of H3K27 of the ZRS.
source: These data suggest that GABPα regulates Shh expression by modulating the acetylation status of H3K27 of the ZRS.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing GABPα overexpression increases H3K27ac and Shh expression.

claim: Both GABPα and p300 are released from the ZRS when FGF signalling is inhibited by NIN and the enhancer is no longer poised.
source: Furthermore, FGF signalling plays a central role, since both GABPα and p300 are released from the ZRS when FGF signalling is inhibited by NIN and the enhancer is no longer poised (Figure 4D–E).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D-E.

claim: FGF mediates priming of the ZRS enabling the binding of GABPα which, in turn, recruits p300.
source: FGF, therefore, mediates priming of the ZRS enabling the binding of GABPα which, in turn, recruits p300.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing FGF is required for H3K4me1, GABPα binding, and p300 recruitment.

claim: ETV4/ETV5 binding acts as repressors to restrict Shh expression outside the ZPA.
source: Occupancy at multiple GABPα/ETS1 sites in the ZRS regulates the position of the ZPA boundary, whereas ETV4/ETV5 binding acts as repressors to restrict expression outside the ZPA.
evidence: This is supported by previous work cited.

claim: HDAC2 appeared significantly enriched over the ZRS in 14Fp cells.
source: Most of the HDACs represented were subjected to ChIP in 14Fp (HDAC1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 9) and HDAC2 appeared significantly enriched over the ZRS (data not shown) and is one of the most abundant Hdac in the RNA samples analysed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP experiments and RNA-seq data.

claim: Hdac1 downregulation had no effect on Shh expression, while the reduction of Hdac2 levels in 14Fp showed an increase in Shh levels.
source: Hdac1 downregulation had no effect on Shh expression, while the reduction of Hdac2 levels (by siRNA) in 14Fp showed an increase in Shh levels.
evidence: This is supported by siRNA knockdown and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Simultaneous reduction of both Hdac1 and Hdac2 did not have an additive effect on the induction of Shh.
source: Simultaneous reduction of both Hdac1 and Hdac2 did not have an additive effect on the induction of Shh (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by siRNA knockdown and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: ETV4 exhibits two peaks encompassing the ZRS which correspond to the two ETV4 binding sites.
source: ETV4 exhibits two peaks encompassing the ZRS which correspond to the two ETV4 binding sites (Lettice et al., 2012); interestingly, the HDAC2 peak overlapped one of these peaks located at the 3' end which encodes the long-range activity of the regulatory element (Lettice et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The HDAC2 peak overlapped one of the ETV4 peaks located at the 3' end which encodes the long-range activity of the regulatory element.
source: ETV4 exhibits two peaks encompassing the ZRS which correspond to the two ETV4 binding sites (Lettice et al., 2012); interestingly, the HDAC2 peak overlapped one of these peaks located at the 3' end which encodes the long-range activity of the regulatory element (Lettice et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Endogenous ETV4 co-immunoprecipitated with HDAC2.
source: We next tested if HDAC2 and ETV4 were able to physically interact; analysis showed that endogenous ETV4 co-immunoprecipitated with HDAC2 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Etv4 levels were reduced with siRNA, resulting in a ~40% decrease in ETV4 and a significant activation of Shh expression.
source: Etv4 levels were reduced with siRNA, resulting in a ~40% decrease in ETV4 and a significant activation of Shh expression (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by siRNA knockdown and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: ChIP using anti-ETV4 and HDAC2 antibodies performed on TSA treated cells showed that ETV4 together with HDAC2 are displaced from the ZRS.
source: ChIP using anti-ETV4 and HDAC2 antibodies performed on TSA treated cells showed that ETV4 together with HDAC2 are displaced from the ZRS (Figure 6E), suggesting that ETV4 opposes GABPα activity by maintaining lower levels of H3K27ac.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: ETV4 opposes GABPα activity by maintaining lower levels of H3K27ac.
source: ChIP using anti-ETV4 and HDAC2 antibodies performed on TSA treated cells showed that ETV4 together with HDAC2 are displaced from the ZRS (Figure 6E), suggesting that ETV4 opposes GABPα activity by maintaining lower levels of H3K27ac.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing ETV4 interacts with HDAC2 and is displaced upon activation.

claim: An initial input is the event that primes the ZRS, such that the enhancer is poised but transcriptionally inactive.
source: We showed that an initial input is the event that primes the ZRS, such that the enhancer is poised but transcriptionally inactive.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The ZRS priming occurs in a broad region of the distal limb bud mesenchyme that includes tissue that will not express Shh in addition to the ZPA.
source: The ZRS priming occurs in a broad region of the distal limb bud mesenchyme that includes tissue that will not express Shh in addition to the ZPA.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data showing H3K4me1 enrichment in both anterior and posterior distal limb.

claim: Distal limb mesenchyme, referred to as the progress zone, is known to be under the influence of the FGFs produced in the AER.
source: Distal limb mesenchyme, referred to as the progress zone, is known to be under the influence of the FGFs produced in the AER (Laufer et al., 1994; Niswander et al., 1994; Crossley et al., 1996; Vogel et al., 1996; Ohuchi et al., 1997) and we showed that FGFs can induce ZRS priming in distal mesenchyme; whereas, inhibition of FGF signalling results in chromatin changes and loss of H3K4me1 and loss of transcription factor binding suggesting that the ZRS is no longer recognized as a poised enhancer and is in a 'closed' configuration.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: FGFs can induce ZRS priming in distal mesenchyme.
source: Distal limb mesenchyme, referred to as the progress zone, is known to be under the influence of the FGFs produced in the AER (Laufer et al., 1994; Niswander et al., 1994; Crossley et al., 1996; Vogel et al., 1996; Ohuchi et al., 1997) and we showed that FGFs can induce ZRS priming in distal mesenchyme; whereas, inhibition of FGF signalling results in chromatin changes and loss of H3K4me1 and loss of transcription factor binding suggesting that the ZRS is no longer recognized as a poised enhancer and is in a 'closed' configuration.
evidence: This is supported by data showing FGF treatment of proximal limb induces H3K4me1 at the ZRS.

claim: Inhibition of FGF signalling results in chromatin changes and loss of H3K4me1 and loss of transcription factor binding suggesting that the ZRS is no longer recognized as a poised enhancer and is in a 'closed' configuration.
source: Distal limb mesenchyme, referred to as the progress zone, is known to be under the influence of the FGFs produced in the AER (Laufer et al., 1994; Niswander et al., 1994; Crossley et al., 1996; Vogel et al., 1996; Ohuchi et al., 1997) and we showed that FGFs can induce ZRS priming in distal mesenchyme; whereas, inhibition of FGF signalling results in chromatin changes and loss of H3K4me1 and loss of transcription factor binding suggesting that the ZRS is no longer recognized as a poised enhancer and is in a 'closed' configuration.
evidence: This is supported by data showing FGF inhibition reduces H3K4me1 and transcription factor binding.

claim: One role of FGF signalling is the establishment and maintenance of ZRS priming.
source: Thus, one role of FGF signalling is the establishment and maintenance of ZRS priming.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on FGF effects on H3K4me1 at the ZRS.

claim: Activation of the ZRS appears to be a two-step process; ZRS priming occurring broadly in the distal mesenchyme which is a prerequisite for subsequent action by other signals in the posterior region containing the ZPA to activate the ZRS.
source: Activation of the ZRS, therefore, appears to be a two-step process; ZRS priming occurring broadly in the distal mesenchyme which is a prerequisite for subsequent action by other signals in the posterior region containing the ZPA to activate the ZRS.
evidence: This is a model inferred from the data showing differential H3K4me1 and H3K27ac patterns.

claim: The poised state of the enhancer is notable in light of the response of the ZRS to the point mutations that cause PPD2 and other associated skeletal abnormalities.
source: The poised state of the enhancer is notable in light of the response of the ZRS to the point mutations that cause PPD2 and other associated skeletal abnormalities (Anderson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a discussion point connecting the findings to previous work on mutations.

claim: ZRS mutations cause misregulation of Shh expression in the developing limb bud such that Shh expression occurs at an ectopic anterior site in the distal mesenchyme in addition to the ZPA.
source: These mutations cause misregulation of Shh expression in the developing limb bud such that Shh expression occurs at an ectopic anterior site in the distal mesenchyme in addition to the ZPA.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on ZRS mutations.

claim: Ectopic expression of all ZRS mutations examined is restricted to the distal mesenchyme suggesting that there is a requirement for the ZRS to be in a poised state in order to be activated.
source: Ectopic expression of all ZRS mutations examined, thus far, is restricted to the distal mesenchyme suggesting that there is a requirement for the ZRS to be in a poised state in order to be activated and demonstrates a mechanism for Shh ectopic activation restricted to the distal mesenchyme of the limb bud.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that mutations only cause ectopic expression in the distal mesenchyme where the ZRS is poised.

claim: 3C assay revealed a physical interaction between the ZRS and the Shh promoter in the limb bud.
source: In the limb bud, 3C assay revealed a physical interaction between the ZRS and the promoter (Amano et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Upon activation of Shh expression in the limb-derived cell line, there is highly specific co-localization of the ZRS with the Shh promoter fragment.
source: Here, we confirmed, that upon activation of Shh expression in the limb-derived cell line, there is highly specific co-localization of the ZRS with the Shh promoter fragment.
evidence: This is supported by 4C-seq data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The Shh limb regulator in the cell line exists in two states; one in which the ZRS is poised reflecting its origin from the distal mesenchyme of the developing limb bud and secondly, in an active state in which the ZRS and the promoter recruit Pol II and interact.
source: Thus, the Shh limb regulator in the cell line exists in two states; one in which the ZRS is poised reflecting its origin from the distal mesenchyme of the developing limb bud and secondly, in an active state in which the ZRS and the promoter recruit Pol II and interact.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the ChIP and 4C data.

claim: GABPα and ETV4 bind to the ZRS in the cell lines similar to that in the limb bud.
source: We have hypothesized that the balance between these activator and repressor factors is responsible for regulating activity levels in the developing limb bud (Lettice et al., 2012). Here, we showed that GABPα and ETV4 bind to the ZRS in the cell lines similar to that in the limb bud.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data in the cell line.

claim: GABPα is associated with p300 HAT at the ZRS in the cell lines.
source: GABPα is associated with p300 HAT at the ZRS in the cell lines.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-on-chip data showing co-localization.

claim: GABPα physically interacts with p300 in myeloid cells.
source: Previous reports demonstrated that GABPα physically interacts with p300 in myeloid cells (Resendes and Rosmarin, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Activation of AChR gene in subsynaptic nuclei in adult skeletal muscle is mediated by GABPα, which recruits the HAT p300 to the AChR ε-subunit promoter.
source: Activation of AChR (nicotinic acetylcholine receptor) gene in subsynaptic nuclei in adult skeletal muscle is mediated by GABPα, which recruits the HAT p300 to the AChR ε-subunit promoter (Ravel-Chapuis et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The surface of the GABPα OST domain binds to the CH1 and CH3 domains of the co-activator HAT CBP/p300.
source: Furthermore, the surface of the GABPα OST domain binds to the CH1 and CH3 domains of the co-activator HAT CBP/p300 (Kang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Expression of Gabpα results in a displacement of ETV4 at the enhancer.
source: A correlation between Gabpα expression and the presence of ETV4 at the ZRS is also observed; in that, expression of Gabpα results in a displacement of ETV4 at the enhancer.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data after GABPα overexpression shown in Figure 5F.

claim: GABPα operates at the ZRS to increase levels of H3K27ac by recruiting p300 and decreasing levels of the repressor ETV4.
source: Thus GABPα operates at the ZRS to increase levels of H3K27ac by recruiting p300 and decreasing levels of the repressor ETV4.
evidence: This is a summary statement inferred from the combined data on GABPα effects.

claim: ETV4 appears to operate in the opposite manner and is one of the dominant factors in maintaining the ZRS in a poised state.
source: ETV4 appears to operate in the opposite manner and is one of the dominant factors in maintaining the ZRS in a poised state.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing ETV4 knockdown activates Shh.

claim: Reduction of ETV4 levels is sufficient to activate Shh expression.
source: Reduction of ETV4 levels is sufficient to activate Shh expression.
evidence: This is supported by siRNA knockdown data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: ETV4 interacts with HDAC2.
source: ETV4 interacts with HDAC2 and we further showed the co-localization of HDAC2 and ETV4 at the ZRS in the cell line.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Knockdown of HDAC2 induces Shh.
source: Similar to the downregulation of ETV4 the knockdown of HDAC2 induces Shh.
evidence: This is supported by siRNA knockdown data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Activation of Shh by TSA releases ETV4 and HDAC2 from the ZRS.
source: Activation of Shh by TSA releases ETV4 and HDAC2 from the ZRS.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data after TSA treatment shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Activation of the ZRS by both the overexpression of GABPα and treatment with TSA is associated with loss of ETV4 binding which acts directly on HDAC activity.
source: Hence activation of the ZRS by both the overexpression of GABPα and treatment with TSA is associated with loss of ETV4 binding which acts directly on HDAC activity.
evidence: This is a summary statement inferred from the combined data.

claim: The FGFs play a central role in Shh expression by ensuring that the ZRS maintains its primed state throughout the distal limb mesenchyme.
source: The FGFs play a central role in Shh expression by ensuring that the ZRS maintains its primed state throughout the distal limb mesenchyme.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the FGF inhibition and treatment experiments.

claim: Widespread priming opens the ZRS for potential ectopic activation as occurs in preaxial polydactyly and associated phenotypes.
source: This widespread priming, however, opens the ZRS for potential ectopic activation as occurs in preaxial polydactyly and associated phenotypes (Anderson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that the ZRS is poised throughout the distal mesenchyme.

claim: ETV4 is a repressor that restricts ZRS activity and FGF signalling induces the levels of ETV4 in the distal mesenchyme of the limb bud.
source: ETV4 is a repressor that restricts this activity and FGF signalling also induces the levels of ETV4 in the distal mesenchyme of the limb bud (Mao et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The FGFs operate by regulating two contrasting events; firstly, by effecting the chromatin in the distal mesenchyme ensuring that the ZRS is maintained in a poised state and secondly, acting counter to enhancer activation by inducing the level of a repressor that ensures Shh expression does not occur outside the region of the ZPA.
source: The FGFs, therefore, operate by regulating two contrasting events; firstly, by effecting the chromatin in the distal mesenchyme ensuring that the ZRS is maintained in a poised state and secondly, acting counter to enhancer activation by inducing the level of a repressor that ensures Shh expression does not occur outside the region of the ZPA.
evidence: This is a summary model inferred from the combined data on FGF effects.

claim: The 14Fp cell line was derived from the posterior third of distal forelimb buds from an Immortomouse.
source: The 14Fp cell line was derived from the posterior third of distal forelimb buds from an Immortomouse (H-2k-tsA58) (Jat et al., 1991).
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the cell line origin.

claim: Elevated frequencies of Shh/ZRS co-localization were observed only in the Shh expressing regions of the limb bud.
source: Elevated frequencies of Shh/ZRS co-localization were observed only in the Shh expressing regions of the limb bud (Amano et al., 2009), in a conformation consistent with enhancer-promoter loop formation (Williamson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The domain between Shh and ZRS is highly compacted in all tissues and developmental stages analysed independent of Shh expression.
source: However, the domain between Shh and ZRS is highly compacted in all tissues and developmental stages analysed independent of Shh expression.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The ZRS contains two domains with distinct activities; one domain, the 5' end of the ZRS (472 bp), directs the spatiotemporal activity and the second domain, the 3' half (308 bp), is required to mediate activity over long genomic distances.
source: Previously, we showed that the ZRS contains two domains with distinct activities; one domain, the 5' end of the ZRS (472 bp), directs the spatiotemporal activity and the second domain, the 3' half (308 bp), is required to mediate activity over long genomic distances (Lettice et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Two different human PPD2 point mutations generate additional ETS binding sites, thereby, de-repressing expression of Shh in the anterior limb bud.
source: For example, two different human PPD2 point mutations generate additional ETS binding sites, thereby, de-repressing expression of Shh in the anterior limb bud.
evidence: This is supported by previous work on mutations.

claim: The balance between binding of the activators and repressors is crucial for normal Shh expression and the mutations that disrupt this balance result in skeletal defects.
source: The balance between binding of the activators and repressors is crucial for normal Shh expression and the mutations that disrupt this balance result in skeletal defects.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by previous work on mutations.
